beats.narration_says: Every cargo that came off a Carthaginian ship was counted twice. Once by the captain who brought it, and once by a clerk who had never been to sea.
beats.viewer_sees: A clerk reading back his own tally on the quay, then the wax itself, cut column by column.

STYLE: detailed hand-drawn 2D historical animation illustration, clean dark outlines, expressive stylized characters, layered environments, 16:9.
SUBJECT: Hanno, a lean Carthaginian clerk of about fifty, close-cropped grey hair, a short curled beard, an undyed linen tunic belted with rope, a wax tablet under one arm.
DETAIL: at this distance the detail belongs to the face and the hands — the crease held between the brows, the ink-dark thumbnail, the rope belt knotted twice at the hip; the quay stones stay broad and simple behind him.
WEARING/PROPS: worn leather sandals, a bronze stylus tucked behind one ear.
ACTION: he stands over the open tablet and reads the last column back to himself.
SETTING: a long stone quay of fitted limestone blocks, crates and amphorae stacked along its edge.
CAMERA: camera stands two paces from him on the quay, eye level, medium.
FRAME LAYOUT: left third — Hanno, near-camera and large; center — the open tablet held at chest height; right third — a moored hull, far and hazy.
FACING: we see his face and chest three-quarter on, his eyes down on the wax.
SCREEN DIRECTION: a gull's shadow slides across the lower-left stones and off the frame.
LIGHT: flat morning haze off the water, no hard shadows anywhere.
PALETTE: sand ochre, weathered timber, sea green.
NOT IN FRAME: the city walls, the open sea, any written number.

beats.narration_says: The jars themselves carried the record. One stroke at the shoulder for one count, and the wax seal to say the count was closed.
beats.viewer_sees: The marks on the sealed jars, the room that holds them, and the clerk putting the day away.
